_meta.purpose: Hand-curated ground-truth anchor points for rarity-pill calibration. Replaces the iNat-circular backtest with externally-sourced visitor encounter probabilities pulled from peer-reviewed studies, NPS operational reports, long-term ecological monitoring outputs, and well-documented field-guide consensus. Each anchor is a (parkId, species, expected probability) triple at a specific season + visit-effort context.
_meta.scoring: scripts/calibrateAgainstAnchors.js loads this file, looks each species up in the static cache, computes the model's predicted probability for the matched (season, effort) context, and reports Ranked Probability Score (Epstein 1969) plus a reliability diagram. RPS is proper and distance-sensitive — predicting `exceptional` when truth is `likely` is penalized more than predicting `unlikely`.

anchorSchema.species: common name as used in the cache (case-sensitive)
anchorSchema.season: spring | summer | fall | winter | year-round (year-round means averaged across all seasons)
anchorSchema.visitorEffort: casual (default) | expert | drive (matches the popup effort selector)
anchorSchema.probability: anchor encounter probability (0-1) — the externally-attested chance of seeing this species on a typical visit in the named context
anchorSchema.tierExpected: guaranteed | very_likely | likely | unlikely | rare | exceptional — derived from probability via RARITY_THRESHOLDS
anchorSchema.confidence: high | medium | low — how directly the source measures per-visit visitor encounter (high = explicit visitor-survey or operational sighting log; medium = trusted field-guide consensus or ecological monitoring; low = inferred from related metrics)
anchorSchema.rationale: 1-2 sentence note on why this anchor is trustworthy and any caveats

_meta.zoneSchemaNote: When `zone` is set, the calibration script uses the species' zone-specific rarity (animal.zones[zone]) instead of the park-level rarity. Zone IDs match src/data/parkZones.js.

anchors.source: Lake Clark NPS coastal raptor sightings — Cook Inlet / Tuxedni Bay.
anchors.rationale: Bald Eagles fish the salmon-rich coastal waters; visible to nearly every flightseeing or coastal-tour visitor in summer.

anchors.source: Virgin Islands NPS coastal seabird reports.
anchors.rationale: Brown Pelicans at Trunk Bay, Cinnamon Bay, and every snorkel beach year-round.

anchors.source: American Samoa NPS shorebird inventories.
anchors.rationale: Reef herons reliably visible along Tutuila and Ofu coastal tide pools.

anchors.source: Congaree NPS boardwalk / Harry Hampton visitor center sightings.
anchors.rationale: Squirrels reliably visible from the boardwalk and visitor center grounds.

anchors.source: Gateway Arch NPS urban park bird sightings.
anchors.rationale: Robins on every Arch grounds lawn and tree year-round (urban park standard).

anchors.source: Great Sand Dunes NPS visitor sightings — every overlook + dune-field area.
anchors.rationale: Ravens patrol the dune-field, parking lots, and overlooks year-round.

anchors.source: Black Canyon NPS South Rim overlook visitor sightings.
anchors.rationale: Ravens patrol Painted Wall, Sunset View, and every South Rim overlook.

anchors.source: Canyonlands NPS Island in the Sky / Needles visitor sightings.
anchors.rationale: Deer along the access roads and at developed campgrounds; not a routine sighting at every visit.

anchors.source: Mesa Verde NPS Morefield / Far View wildlife reports.
anchors.rationale: Turkey flocks regularly visible in Morefield Campground and forest-edge areas.

anchors.source: North Cascades NPS Hwy 20 corridor visitor sightings.
anchors.rationale: Ravens at Diablo Lake / Ross Lake overlooks and along the highway corridor.

anchors.source: Gates of the Arctic NPS expedition trip wildlife reports.
anchors.rationale: Bald Eagles fish the Brooks Range river corridors during summer salmon runs — visible to ~half of expedition trips.

anchors.source: Kobuk Valley NPS Kobuk River wildlife reports.
anchors.rationale: Bald Eagles patrol the Kobuk River salmon runs in summer — reliable for flightseeing / float trips.

anchors.source: Wrangell-St Elias NPS McCarthy Road / Nabesna Road wildlife sightings.
anchors.rationale: Moose visible along the McCarthy Road and Nabesna Road willows in summer.

anchors.source: Guadalupe Mountains NPS Pine Springs / McKittrick Canyon visitor sightings.
anchors.rationale: Ravens at Pine Springs visitor center, Guadalupe Peak trail, and McKittrick Canyon — every developed area.

anchors.source: Haleakala NPS lower-elevation visitor area sightings.
anchors.rationale: Mynas at Hosmer Grove and Park Headquarters lawn (lower elevation); less common at summit.
